terms.grammar: pronoun: genitive plural of is (eōrum masculine and neuter, eārum feminine)
terms.comment: When the owners are not the subject: Manlius was woken clangōre eōrum, by the geese’s honking. It follows the owners’ gender: vōx eārum, the sheep’s voice.

evidence: Liv. 21.58.8: tegminibus suīs magis obrutī quam tēctī
terms.comment: When the owners are the subject: the men lay tegminibus suīs … obrutī, buried by their own shields. The same word serves for his, her, its and their.

phrases.latin: namque clangōre eōrum ālārumque crepitū excitus M. Mānlius
phrases.english: for Marcus Manlius, woken by their honking and the flapping of their wings

phrases.latin: vōx eārum nōn mē, sed bē sonāre vidētur
phrases.english: Their voice seems to sound not “meh” but “beh”.

phrases.latin: nē, quās ibi posuerīs ad partum, nōn līberōs eārum, sed ipsās quaerās
phrases.english: so that you aren’t looking for the snails you put there to breed, rather than their young

phrases.latin: tantum nivōsae grandinis dējēcit ut omnibus omissīs procumberent hominēs tegminibus suīs magis obrutī quam tēctī
phrases.english: It threw down so much snowy hail that the men let everything go and lay down, buried rather than covered by their shields.

phrases.latin: Gallī occursant in rīpā cum variīs ululātibus cantūque mōris suī, quatientēs scūta super capita
phrases.english: The Gauls rush to meet them on the bank with all kinds of howls and singing in their own fashion, shaking their shields over their heads.

phrases.latin: nostrī namque Gallī ventum ex suā terrā flantem, quem saevissimum patiuntur, circium appellant ā turbine, opīnor, ejus ac vertīgine
phrases.english: For our Gauls call the wind that blows from their own land, which they find the fiercest, circius, from its whirling and turning, I think.

sources: Lewis & Short: is · Lewis & Short: suus · Lewis & Short: ille
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius, loci-livius, loci-varro), checked against the editions named there.
